name: BackcountryAI
tagline: A field guide you can talk to, with no signal.
subtitle: Offline survival and first aid
pitch: Describe what's happening in your own words. The app finds the right passages in a library stored on your iPhone and writes a step-by-step answer on the phone itself, with citations. Nothing is sent anywhere, so it works in Airplane Mode.
privacy: No account, no tracking, no data collected.
status: In TestFlight beta. Not on the App Store yet

features.title: Answers you can check
features.text: Every answer lists the articles it came from. Tap a citation to read the original. When something isn't in the library, the app says so.

features.title: A library that lives on your phone
features.text: 277,000 articles in one download of about 0.8 GB, from sources like the National Park Service, National Weather Service, CDC, FEMA and U.S. Army field manuals.

features.title: Built for emergencies
features.text: SOS on every chat screen, one-tap guides for bleeding, hypothermia, burns, fractures and more, and a field mode with a patient assessment, vitals log and SOAP note for rescuers.

features.title: Battery-aware
features.text: See what each answer cost, save answers to reread for free, and search the whole library with no AI and almost no battery.

features.title: Better answers, still offline
features.text: An optional larger on-device model (2.3 GB) gives more specific answers on iPhones with enough memory.

features.title: Trail ready
features.text: A checklist confirms everything works offline before you leave.

engineering.intro: A SwiftUI app where retrieval and generation both run on the device. Apple's Foundation Models writes the answers by default, and the library is a read-only SQLite full-text index.

facts.v: on-device models: Apple's, an embedder and a reranker, plus an optional 4B LLM

points.title: Retrieval on the phone
points.text: Keyword search runs on SQLite FTS5. When they are downloaded, a small embedding model and a reranker find passages by meaning, and search falls back to keywords when they aren't.

points.title: Two answer engines behind one interface
points.text: Apple's Foundation Models is the default. Devices with enough memory can download Qwen 3.5 4B and run it through MLX, behind the same engine protocol.

points.title: Downloads that finish without the app
points.text: The library and the larger model ship as Apple-hosted Background Assets packs. A downloader extension lets iOS fetch them while the app is closed, and a Live Activity shows progress.

points.title: Licensing checked on every release
points.text: The library uses only content that can be redistributed commercially: U.S. government public-domain works and CC BY-SA sources. A script enforces the rules before each release.

points.title: Release from a push
points.text: Every push to main runs the tests and ships a TestFlight build with fastlane. App Store screenshots and the preview video are generated by UI tests from a sample of the real library.

points.title: A command-line twin
points.text: A macOS tool reuses the app's retrieval and engine code to check answer quality and build the search index.
